job.style: a short story with Indian characters in everyday life

passage: Rohan and his sister Meera were observing a pond near their village in Bihar. They saw a frog laying a mass of eggs in the water, while a male frog released sperm over them. Meera asked if the frog needed to stay alive to reproduce. Rohan explained that reproduction is for the survival of the species, not the individual. He pointed out that the tiny sperm and the larger egg are both single cells, essential for creating a new life. As they watched, the fertilised egg became a single-celled zygote. Rohan noted that the zygote is not a miniature frog yet; it must divide into many cells to form an embryo. Later, this embryo develops into a tadpole, which looks nothing like the adult frog. The tadpole undergoes metamorphosis, a dramatic change in body structure, to become an adult. Meera wondered if other animals like humans also lay eggs. Rohan clarified that humans are viviparous, meaning they give birth to young ones, unlike the oviparous frogs. He reminded her that the embryo in humans receives nutrients from the mother, not from the sperm. They realised that life cycles are complex and unique to each species, ensuring that nature continues its cycle through these diverse methods of reproduction.

items.evidence: Rohan explained that reproduction is for the survival of the species, not the individual.
items.q: Why does a frog reproduce, if it can stay alive without doing so?
options: So that its kind keeps going on Earth
So that it can live longer itself
So that it can grow into an adult
So that its tadpole can feed on it
items.explain: Reproduction is for the survival of the species, not the individual animal.

wrong.why: thinks reproduction keeps the individual alive
makes up a link between tadpole and parent

items.evidence: He pointed out that the tiny sperm and the larger egg are both single cells, essential for creating a new life.
items.q: Meera says sperm are too tiny to be cells. What does Rohan's point show?
options: Even tiny sperm are whole single cells
Only the larger egg is a real cell
Sperm are cells only after joining the egg
Sperm are a liquid that carries cells
items.explain: Both the tiny sperm and the larger egg are single cells, whatever their size.

wrong.why: thinks small or liquid things are not cells
thinks sperm become cells only after fertilisation
thinks sperm are liquid, not cells

items.evidence: Rohan noted that the zygote is not a miniature frog yet; it must divide into many cells to form an embryo.
items.q: What would Rohan see if he looked at the zygote under a microscope?
options: One cell that has not yet divided
A tiny frog with legs and eyes
A tadpole swimming inside the egg
A ball of many cells with a tail
items.explain: The zygote is a single cell; it must divide many times before it forms an embryo.

wrong.why: thinks the zygote already looks like the parent
skips the embryo stage and jumps to the tadpole
confuses the zygote with a developed embryo

items.evidence: The tadpole undergoes metamorphosis, a dramatic change in body structure, to become an adult.
items.q: How is metamorphosis different from a tadpole simply growing bigger?
options: Its body structure changes into a new form
Its body stays the same but gets longer
Its body gets more cells but keeps its shape
Its body forms a new zygote inside
items.explain: Metamorphosis is a dramatic change in body structure, not just an increase in size.

wrong.why: thinks metamorphosis is just growing bigger
confuses it with cell division in the embryo
mixes it up with early development stages

items.evidence: He reminded her that the embryo in humans receives nutrients from the mother, not from the sperm.
items.q: A child says a human baby is fed by its father's sperm. What is wrong?
options: The embryo gets its food from the mother
The embryo makes all its own food
The embryo gets food from the egg only
The embryo gets food from the water
items.explain: The human embryo receives nutrients from the mother, not from the sperm.

wrong.why: still thinks the father supplies the food
thinks the embryo needs no outside food
